title: Exhibition advertising
slide_intent: Teach designers to adjust the relationship between type, tinted artwork and ground so the exhibition title remains readable across color variants.
strategic_value: The Lines of Beauty campaign can keep its title hierarchy across both a brighter and a quieter color treatment.
demonstration: Two wide adverts superimpose a centered title on tinted drawing details. The upper version uses black on a red field and the lower version uses white on a dark green field.
practical_value: Test both text-and-image combinations with the venue, dates and credits in place before selecting the campaign color.

content_islands.name: Red variant
content_islands.spec: Set the dates, venue identifier and seal across the top. Center the black exhibition name over the tinted drawing and align credits along the foot.

content_islands.name: Dark variant
content_islands.spec: Repeat the horizontal format in dark green with white text. Preserve both the centered title block and the peripheral identifiers.

reference_purposes.Expression: Two exhibition adverts compare warm red artwork with black type against dark green artwork with white type.
reference_purposes.Application: The variants carry the same campaign hierarchy, dates, venue and credits in a wide advertising format.

ingredient.name: Exhibition image tint and type color
ingredient.role: Let a campaign change its color treatment while retaining a readable title hierarchy.
ingredient.application: The shown variants pair black type with a red-tinted drawing and white type with a dark-green drawing. Compare the whole advert with identifiers and credits in place.
ingredient.scope: Two indicative Lines of Beauty campaign variants. Their color pairings are observed examples, not a requirement for other exhibitions.
